sonnet.problem: Papa Dorin says 'I hit snooze for five extra minutes and feel guilty all morning' as if it were his own routine. The snooze button is outside his bakery, so it should come up as something people do, not something he does.
sonnet.rule: Things outside his bakery, like a phone or a car, come up as things people do: "You know when your phone…"

sonnet.problem: Card 5 already jokes that the crown is fancier than his chef's hat. Card 7 makes the same joke again, with the gold crown set against his own humble worth (the 25-cent bin). It is one comparison used twice in one lesson.
sonnet.rule: Each joke idea, comparison and punchline shape is used once per lesson.

sonnet.problem: The right answer 'the Most High' is the only God-title among the answers. The wrong answers 'his people' and 'his nobles' are both groups of people. So the right answer is a different kind of thing and sounds more like the Bible than the others, and it stands out.
sonnet.rule: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. / Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
